pull_requests.title: fix(ffe): stop ordinary winner exposures while preserving holdouts
pull_requests.body:
## Motivation and Context

Implements the winner-logging decision in [RFC: Classifying allocations for per-subject experimentation opt-out](https://docs.google.com/document/d/153tRlj46l-XfBGCA2X_NvxW4vwYObaH8zm2moP_AqMk/edit), including **Handling holdouts using existing doLog**.

The agreed design reuses `doLog` for experimentation opt-out. Ordinary winners stop logging exposures; generated holdouts continue logging. Today, the retained experiment link keeps ordinary winners at `doLog=true`, so opted-out subjects skip them.

### PR stack order

**Position:** Stack A, first PR. Solid arrows show Git parent → child. The dashed arrow shows a deployment prerequisite, not a Git parent.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph A["Stack A: immediate opt-out compiler support"]
        W["#139368: winner logging (this PR)"] --> F["#139379: retain fallbacks"]
    end
    subgraph B["Stack B: stable activation metadata"]
        V["#139367: RC validation"] --> P["#139381: persist and publish"]
    end
    M["k8s-resources #12479: nullable storage"] -.-> P
```

| Stack goal | Review and merge order | Why stacked |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **A: preserve ordinary delivery during immediate opt-out.** | [#139368](https://github.com/ddoghq/dd-source/pull/139368) → [#139379](https://github.com/ddoghq/dd-source/pull/139379) | Correct winner classification first. The fallback optimizer then uses that classification to retain skippable experiments' fallbacks. |
| **B: provide stable activation times for future-experiments-only mode.** | [#139367](https://github.com/ddoghq/dd-source/pull/139367) → [#139381](https://github.com/ddoghq/dd-source/pull/139381) | Separate schema acceptance from emission, so validators can deploy before producers. |

Both stacks start from `main` and can progress independently. [Migration #12479](https://github.com/ddoghq/k8s-resources/pull/12479) targets `k8s-resources/master`. Deploy it and RC validation before #139381; merging alone is insufficient.

## Description

- Read standard experiment lifecycle state in the compiler's existing database snapshot.
- Stop ordinary winner exposures after `ROLLOUT_COMPLETE` or `CODE_REMOVED`, without removing the experiment link.
- Keep generated holdout exposures, serial IDs, assignments, and analysis inclusion unchanged. Canary and bandit logging remain unchanged.
- Preserve logging when lifecycle state is missing. Use one organization-scoped bulk query.

After winner selection, the compiler keeps the two purposes separate:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    C["Completed standard experiment; experiment link retained"] --> W["Ordinary winner allocation: doLog = false"]
    C --> H["Generated holdout allocation, when applicable: doLog = true"]
    W --> D["Winner remains available to opted-out subjects"]
    H --> A["Existing holdout exposures and analysis continue"]
```

This changes exposure logging, not evaluation telemetry.

### Later stacks: preview

These are planned follow-up groups, not additional published PRs in this series.

| Order | Goal | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **C: complete activation coverage** | Establish usable activation metadata for supported allocation types. | Remaining lifecycle writers, canary/bandit coverage where supported, holdout timing, and missing-metadata behavior. |
| **D: shared fixtures and evaluators** | Apply the same cutoff rule locally and at the edge. | Timestamp fixtures first; Go/Rust evaluators, JSON/archive compatibility, Precompute transport, and cache handling. |
| **E: SDK delivery** | Let customers select future-experiments-only behavior consistently. | Extend existing opt-out integrations, pass the customer cutoff, and test request acknowledgement and cached-state compatibility. |

The existing immediate-mode SDK work does not wait for C–E. Future-mode enablement requires completed producer/consumer support and end-to-end validation; these five PRs do not enable it.

## How has this been tested?

The full UFC suite passed. Regression tests check 8,192 winner assignments and execute the holdout assignment query for both winners, global/selective holdouts, and primary/preliminary analysis. A negative control confirms that removing holdout exposures breaks primary analysis.

Repository snapshot and handler lifecycle tests compile, but local database setup is blocked by Docker storage errors. They still need a successful CI run. This is not deployed end-to-end proof.

## What is expected of reviewers?

Check that the implementation follows the RFC: only completed standard winners stop logging. Review snapshot consistency, organization scoping, and preservation of holdout metadata and the experiment link.

inline_comments.body:
🤖 **Comment from Claude working with Aaron Silverman:** **[P1]** A concluded standard experiment that still splits traffic now compiles with `doLog=false`, so it randomizes opted-out subjects. Please base opt-out eligibility on randomization, not on `doLog` alone. We want a concluded experiment to behave like a randomized allocation that was never an experiment, and we want opted-out subjects to skip both, because both randomize. The exclusion in #140422 checks only `doLog`, so it skips neither. The RFC reuses `doLog` alone, so this needs a product decision. This line derives `doLog` for standard experiments from experiment state alone. That adds a new way to reach the state above: the deprecated PATCH `experiment_action: CONCLUDED` sets `ROLLOUT_COMPLETE` without rolling out the winner (`experiment_service.go:653`, called from `experiment_handler.go:2584`). The allocation keeps its split and now compiles with `doLog=false`. I put the evaluator-side change in my comment on #140422 at `experimentation.rs:62`.
Evidence — 1. a completed standard experiment that still splits compiles with doLog=false I added a `TestWinnerExposureLifecycle` row at `3e99ba2a`: a standard experiment with `completed: true` and weights 50/50. The compiled allocation has `doLog=false`, and the split stays.
Evidence — 2. callers still send the deprecated field `ffe.experimentation.experiment.patch_lifecycle_deprecated{field:experiment_action}`, summed over the 30 days to 2026-10-21: us1 95, eu1 28, us5 17, us3 13. The handler counts each request before later checks can reject it (`experiment_handler.go:2259-2264`), and the metric records neither the action nor the outcome. So these are requests that set the field, not successful concludes.
Evidence — 3. opted-out subjects are randomized A probe on the #140422 evaluators, in immediate mode, with a `doLog=false` allocation that splits 50/50 between two variations before a fallback: 200 opted-out subjects got `a` 106 and `b` 94, and none reached the fallback. The JSON and archived evaluators agree on every subject.

inline_comments.body:
🤖 **Comment from Claude working with Aaron Silverman:** **[P2]** Update the synthetic-data holdout runner. It still requires `doLog=true` on a concluded winner. `_stage_is_ready` returns false when the ordinary allocation reports `doLog=false`, also after conclusion (`tools/synthetic_data/core/holdout_runner.py:346`). This PR compiles a concluded standard winner with `doLog=false` (`ufc.go:179`), as this test asserts. So a stage never becomes ready while its evaluations include a concluded ordinary allocation with `doLog=false`. `holdout_primary.py:138` calls the same check with every experiment concluded.
Evidence — probe test, before and after - The test below fails at `3e99ba2a`: `_stage_is_ready` returns `False` for concluded winners served with `doLog=false`. - With the fix, it passes. `tests/test_holdout_runner.py`, `tests/test_holdout_primary.py` and the probe pass: 254 tests. - The fix also accepts `doLog=true` after conclusion, so the runner works against a compiler with or without this PR.
Suggested patch — accept a non-logging winner after conclusion ```diff --- a/domains/ffe/tools/synthetic_data/core/holdout_runner.py +++ b/domains/ffe/tools/synthetic_data/core/holdout_runner.py @@ -343,7 +343,8 @@ if result["variant"] != control or result["reason"] != "DEFAULT": return False elif allocation == ordinary: - if not metadata["doLog"]: + # A concluded experiment serves its winner without exposure logging. + if key not in concluded and not metadata["doLog"]: return False if key in concluded and result["variant"] != (config["ship"] or control): return False ``` Add to `tests/test_holdout_runner.py`: ```python def _ordinary(key, variant, do_log): return { "variant": variant, "reason": "TARGETING_MATCH", "metadata": {"doLog": do_log, "allocationKey": f"{key}-allocation", "__dd_split_serial_id": 7}, } def test_concluded_ordinary_winner_without_exposure_logging_is_ready(): runner = _runner() concluded = {key: [_ordinary(key, runner.experiments[key]["ship"] or runner.experiments[key]["variants"][0]["id"], False)] for key in runner.experiments} assert RealisticHoldoutRunner._stage_is_ready(runner, concluded, set(), set(runner.experiments)) ```

inline_comments.body:
Fixed in [d0a2de5b58](https://github.com/ddoghq/dd-source/commit/d0a2de5b58dba158941d2c2f81016276a45ea2c1). The policy is to exclude allocations that randomize; the backend must represent that through the existing `doLog` field. The compiler now sets `doLog=true` when shard selection changes the variation or match/fallthrough outcome, covering completed 50/50 experiments, ordinary percentage splits, and partial enrollment. Deterministic completed winners remain `false`; existing active-experiment, canary, bandit, and holdout logging requirements are preserved. This deliberately enables exposure logging for ordinary randomized allocations. The evaluator predicate and future-mode cutoff rule stay unchanged.

Recorded as [D018](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/blob/656696f84fb83fea87798a0d4151af0f7e2fc16d/contracts/experimentation-opt-out/backend-feedback.md#d018-randomization-is-represented-by-dolog) in [central draft #55](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/pull/55), published at [656696f84f](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/commit/656696f84fb83fea87798a0d4151af0f7e2fc16d), with this [decision thread](https://github.com/ddoghq/dd-source/pull/139368#discussion_r4343813763) and the earlier withdrawn selection retained in provenance.

[Native evidence](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/blob/656696f84fb83fea87798a0d4151af0f7e2fc16d/contracts/experimentation-opt-out/evidence/backend-review-20261022/native-validation.json): 817 compiler tests and 269 database repository tests pass, including 500 independent raw-bucket enumeration cases. Restoring the old `doLog` output fails the three added scenarios above; restoring the fix passes both suites uncached. [Lean evidence](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/blob/656696f84fb83fea87798a0d4151af0f7e2fc16d/contracts/experimentation-opt-out/evidence/backend-review-20261022/model-validation.json): seven new composition theorems, 53 total audited; 313 existing semantic cases and 36 operational cases pass. The Lean abstraction does not prove the native classifier; the native tests cover that boundary.

Deployment still requires the fallback-preserving child and regenerated UFCs. Newly logging allocations without activation metadata retain the existing conservative future-mode exclusion; activation coverage remains a separate rollout obligation.
